newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHEFFIELD UNITED GO ON THE STOCK MARKET.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHEFFIELD UNITED GO ON THE STOCK MARKET.

text.p: English first division club Sheffield United will join the growing number of teams on the stock market after announcing a takeover deal on Wednesday with leisurewear firm Conrad.

The deal values United, one of the leading contenders for promotion to the premier league, at almost 15 million pounds ($25 million). Conrad will be renamed Sheffield United Plc when the takeover is completed.

Conrad are planning a share issue to raise 12.5 million pounds ($20.9 million), part of which will be used to strengthen the playing staff of the ambitious Yorkshire club, managed by former Everton boss Howard Kendall. United are aiming to recapture the premier league spot they lost in 1994.
Soccer clubs are increasingly attractive for investors as lucrative satellite televison deals pump large sums of money into the game.
